subject: Banking
title: The Swiss National Bank Investor
description: A quick win: understand The Swiss National Bank Investor.

hook.text: Switzerland's central bank owns $150 billion in US stocks. It's a major shareholder in Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon.

buildup.text: The SNB buys foreign assets to weaken the Swiss franc. A strong franc hurts Swiss exporters like Nestlé and Rolex.

discovery.text: By selling francs and buying dollars, euros, and stocks, the SNB pushes its currency down.

twist.text: Unlike the Fed, the SNB is publicly traded. You can buy shares in Switzerland's central bank on the stock exchange.

climax.text: A central bank that owns tech stocks and trades on a stock exchange.

punchline.text: Owns Apple stock. Traded on an exchange. Switzerland's central bank is unique.

quiz.question: Why does the Swiss National Bank buy US stocks?
options: To weaken the Swiss franc by selling it for foreign assets
